blocks.h2: McHenry Gas Fireplace Giving You Trouble?
blocks.intro: When the lake breeze turns cold, these are the calls we get:

tiles.h3: It Sat All Summer and Won't Start
tiles.body: Spiders and dust love a pilot tube that hasn't been used since April. A cleaning usually brings it back.

tiles.h3: The Pilot Lights but the Burner Won't
tiles.body: The thermopile may not be making enough power to open the main valve, or the wall switch has failed.
The burner ports are dirty or the logs have shifted, so the gas isn't burning cleanly.
Try new batteries in both the remote and the receiver. If that fails, the receiver may need replacing.
Get outside first. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from there, then call us when it's safe.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Repair, Cleaning and Yearly Service
blocks.intro: Everything on the gas side of your fireplace:

steps.body: We test the thermopile output, the valve and the ignition system, then replace only what failed.
A full cleaning of the burner, pilot assembly and glass, logs set back in place, every fitting leak-tested and the vent termination checked outside.
New gas supply for a fireplace, insert or outdoor fire feature. See [gas line installation](/mchenry/gas-line-installation).

blocks.h2: Fireplaces in McHenry Homes and Lake Houses
blocks.intro: About 3 in 4 McHenry homes were built between 1970 and 2009, so many gas fireplaces here are sealed direct-vent units or older fireplaces converted to gas.

items.h3: Outside Vent Caps Take a Beating
items.body: Direct-vent fireplaces exhaust through a cap on the outside wall. Snow drifts, wasp nests and landscaping can block it, which leads to sooting and shutdowns. We check the cap on every service call.
Fireplaces in lake houses and cabins may go months without use. Mice and insects nest in the firebox and pilot area. Have it checked before you light it for the season.

items.h3: Parts for 20 to 35 Year Old Units
items.body: Original fireplaces in 1990s and 2000s homes can almost always be repaired. Pilots, thermopiles and valves are still widely available.
A fireplace that burns poorly or vents badly can produce carbon monoxide. Test your detectors when you change the clocks.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: My lake house fireplace hasn't run in months. Is it safe to light?
items.preview: Have it checked first. Nests and debris are common after long breaks.
items.answer: It's worth a check first. Insects and mice often nest in the firebox, pilot tube or vent after a long break. A quick service visit clears it and confirms the connections are tight.

items.q: Why does my fireplace turn off after a few minutes?
items.preview: Often a weak thermopile or a blocked vent.
items.answer: A thermopile that's lost output, a dirty pilot flame or a blocked outside vent can all make the safety system shut the fireplace down. We test each one.

items.q: Can snow block my fireplace vent?
items.preview: Yes. Keep the outside cap clear.
items.answer: Yes. If drifting snow covers the vent cap on a direct-vent fireplace, it can't exhaust properly and may shut down or soot up. Keep the cap clear in winter.

items.q: How often should a gas fireplace be serviced?
items.preview: Once a year, before the heating season.
items.answer: Once a year, ideally in September or October, so any weak part shows up before you really need the heat.

items.q: What does gas fireplace repair cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on the part and the model. The price comes before the work.
items.answer: Every repair is priced on what failed and the make of the fireplace. Once we've found the problem, you get a flat-rate number before anything is replaced.
